strengths: Well-motivated empirical analysis: Clear demonstration that existing sparse attention methods fail on reasoning tasks due to error accumulation, with compelling visualizations and root-cause analysis.
Novel observational findings: Systematic identification of cross-head spatial locality and temporal recency locality patterns provides genuine insight into reasoning attention structure.
Strong design methodology: Each component (cross-head aggregation, proportional recency window, infrequent re-selection) is well-justified by the empirical observations rather than being ad-hoc.

Comprehensive experimental validation: Extensive experiments across multiple model families (Qwen3, DeepSeek-R1), reasoning benchmarks (AIME, MATH500, GPQA), and long-context tasks with consistent improvements.

Significant practical results: Achieves 87.5% sparsity on AIME-24 without accuracy loss, maintains generation lengths close to full attention (avoiding 18-103% inflation of baselines), and delivers 1.6× end-to-end speedup.
Thorough ablation studies: Section A.1 validates key design choices (CUSA aggregation robustness, recency window ratio, generation length preservation) with convincing evidence.
Architectural generality: Demonstrated effectiveness on both GQA and MHA models, and generalization to both reasoning and retrieval tasks.
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: The core contribution is relatively incremental—aggregating per-head selections via UnionFlatten and adding proportional recency allocation are straightforward extensions of TidalDecode. More substantial algorithmic innovation is needed.

Shallow theoretical understanding: Paper is primarily empirical without principled explanation for why these attention patterns emerge or mechanistic justification beyond pattern matching. The causality between observed overlap and global token importance is not rigorously established.

Fixed hyperparameters without thorough justification: Recency ratio r=0.25 is static across all models/tasks; generalization beyond AIME-24 (A.1.2) is unclear. Number of full-attention layers (2) and re-selection layers (1) lack principled justification. Re-selection layer varies by model (L12 vs L20) without clear principle.

Modest efficiency gains at practical scales: Only 1.09× speedup at 16K context (common scenario), 1.27× at 32K; full 1.6× speedup only at 64K. Speedup scales with context length, limiting impact in many deployments.

Weaker performance on non-reasoning tasks: LongBench shows smaller margins over TidalDecode (43.82 vs 40.89 at 1K budget); Needle-in-Haystack results match rather than outperform. Suggests optimization for reasoning rather than general long-context tasks.
Insufficient statistical rigor: No error bars or confidence intervals; variance across 64 traces not reported; some results close to baselines lack significance testing.

Incomplete presentation: Algorithm 1 notation (UnionFlatten, TopKIndices) not precisely defined; Figure 2 visualization difficult to parse; code URL appears as placeholder; critical details relegated to appendix.
Limited failure analysis: No discussion of failure modes, cases where head specialization matters, or edge cases where the method underperforms. Generation length distribution/variance not analyzed.

Incomplete baseline comparison: Limited to selection-based sparse attention; no comparison with other efficiency approaches (distillation, quantization); only one training-required baseline; missing recent efficiency methods.
